s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of respiratory and cutaneous symptoms with stridor, wheezing, and hypotension, recurring over several weeks
salient_findings: Wheezing, cough, and swelling of the lips, face, and tongue after ingestion of a nutritional supplement
Stridor, biphasic wheezing, and poor air movement without visible oropharyngeal swelling
Recurring episodes of subjective perioral swelling, hypotension, and stridor without objective edema
key_facts: 14-year-old girl with a history of suspected food allergies and intermittent asthma
Ingestion of a hypoallergenic nutritional supplement triggered the initial episode
Self-administered epinephrine at home prior to ED arrival
Negative skin prick tests and serum-specific IgE to foods of concern except for sensitization to several tree nuts
Normal testing for hereditary angioedema and baseline serum tryptase
Lost 40 lb over the past year through dietary restriction and exercise
Homeschooled due to fears of allergic reactions
Multiple ED evaluations and PICU admissions for similar episodes
Serial serum tryptase levels during acute events remained normal
Direct laryngoscopy showed no airway edema or paradoxical vocal cord motion
Managed with daily antihistamines, ranitidine, cromolyn, and a tapering course of prednisone

shortlist.label: Mast Cell Activation Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Recurring episodes of anaphylaxis-like symptoms without clear allergen exposure, normal serum tryptase levels, and response to antihistamines and corticosteroids

shortlist.label: Idiopathic Anaphylaxis
shortlist.why_kept: Episodes of anaphylaxis without identifiable cause, normal testing for hereditary angioedema, and lack of objective edema on direct laryngoscopy

shortlist.label: Vocal Cord Dysfunction
shortlist.why_kept: Stridor and wheezing without visible oropharyngeal swelling, and lack of airway edema on direct laryngoscopy

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic Esophagitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of food allergies and suspected food-induced reactions, although skin prick tests and serum-specific IgE were largely negative

shortlist.label: Autoimmune Angioedema
shortlist.why_kept: Recurring episodes of angioedema-like symptoms without clear allergen exposure or family history of hereditary angioedema
